newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end largely flat in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end largely flat in quiet trade.

text.p: Swedish shares ended largely flat on Monday in quiet, cautious trade ahead of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on Tuesday.
The exchange's general index rose 0.02 percent to 2,660.54 in turnover of 3.30 billion crowns.
"This day goes to history as completely uninteresting," a broker said.
Gas group AGA belonged to the winners and jumped four crowns to 110, but dealers could not explain the rise.
Telecoms group Ericsson came off day highs when its U.S. share fell and ended 0.5 crown higher at 254.5.
Metals and mining group Trelleborg rose three crowns to 133 on rumours that a brokerage had released a positive report about the company.
Car safety equipment Autoliv jumped ten crowns to 329 after news U.S. tax authorities gave the planned merger between the group and a unit of U.S. Morton a preliminary nod.

The market is expected to remain quiet on Tuesday ahead of the FOMC meeting, when many players expect the Federal Reserve to raise rates. A rate hike has been largely discounted and players are expected to take their cue from Wall Street.
